Per protocol, left/right legs are authored as a single shared internal joint chain (shoulder/knee/fetlock, hip/stifle/hock/fetlock) with the symmetric fork occurring ONLY at the terminal hoof leaves (z sign mirrored using front-view/top-view left-right spread), since symmetric pairs must join two leaves, not internal joints. All lengths converted from grid pixel distances to positive integers; vertical (y) components negated relative to the downward-increasing image grid so that descending limbs have negative dy in the output frame (+y up). Four leg leaves + head + tail = 6 total leaves, matching leaf-count convention.

tree.notes: Frog has no external tail, so only 5 leaves: head + 4 limbs. Root placed at pelvis (hip center). Spine simplified to a single chest/shoulder segment (root->spine1) plus a head segment, since the frog's neck is negligible in the side view (withers-to-head slope read directly from side view). Each limb was split into anatomically standard 3-segment chains (front: shoulder-elbow-wrist-hand; hind: hip-knee-ankle-foot) inferred from the folded-leg silhouette in the side view; lateral (z) placement and splay of each joint was inferred from the top view, where hind legs show a much larger lateral splay (knee/foot offset ≈10) than front legs (elbow/hand offset ≈6-10), consistent with typical frog anatomy where hind legs are proportionally larger and more sprawled. All vertical (y) directions were sign-flipped from the screen's down-positive grid to the up-positive model frame; verified hip->foot and shoulder->hand both have net negative dy (legs descend), confirming correct orientation.

Y-grid coordinates (0=top,24=bottom) were inverted (dy_frame = -(delta y_image)) to satisfy the +Y-up frame convention; e.g. peduncle->tail and shoulder->pect fins all show negative dy, correctly indicating downward-hanging/curving appendages. tree.notes: Starfish has 5 arms + central disc, treated as radially symmetric with one unpaired anterior arm and two bilateral pairs (left/right lateral arms, rear-left/rear-right arms) to satisfy the symmetric-pair rule. Root ('center') is the animal's mouth/central point (length 0). 'disc' is a small internal spine node representing the central body bump (aboral disc) from which all arms radiate - added so the body isn't a single hub, per structure rules. Each arm is modeled as a single segment (base at disc, tip = leaf) since starfish arms taper continuously with no discrete joints like a vertebrate limb (thigh/knee/etc. segmentation not anatomically applicable here); this single-segment choice is the inferred simplification. Lengths were read from the side (XY) view as straight-line distances from the disc center (~12.5,12.5) to each arm tip: anterior tip (12,1)->~11.5≈12; left tip (2,12)->~10.5≈11; right tip (23,12)->~10.5≈11; rear-left tip (8,23)->~11.4≈11; rear-right tip (17,23)->~11.4≈11. The vertical (Y) grid axis runs 0 at top to 24 at bottom on screen, so screen-down = negative real dy per the required flip; this is why the rear-left/rear-right arms (which descend on screen) get negative dy (-0.919) and the anterior arm (which rises on screen) gets positive dy (+0.999). Front (ZY) and top (XZ) views show the star lies almost entirely in the XY plane with only a small, roughly uniform Z thickness (the flat body depth), so Z-components of arm directions were set to ~0 rather than varying per arm.

tree.notes: Octopus has no external tail leaf; mantle/rostrum treated as single 'head' leaf on the midline. The 8 arms were grouped into 4 bilaterally symmetric pairs (front, mid-front, mid-back, back) based on their radial spread in the top (XZ) view; within each pair the true anatomical length is kept equal for both sides even though the render shows different curl poses (proportion, not pose). Each arm was split into base->tip as the minimal inferred multi-segment joint, since the grid only gives base attachment and tip endpoints, not intermediate joints. Vertical directions were flipped per the grid convention (screen-down = physically negative y), giving all arm-tip segments a negative dy since arms droop from the mantle toward the ground, while the head/rostrum direction is slightly positive dy since it points up and forward from the mantle center.

tree.notes: Spider (tarantula-like) mesh, no external tail. Body spine simplified to root(junction of abdomen/cephalothorax)->abdomen(terminal, not a leaf, per convention only appendages/head/tail count as leaves)->cephalothorax->head(leaf). All 8 legs attach at cephalothorax and were each split into 4 inferred segments (coxa-femur-tibia-tarsus) since the grid only gives overall limb span; segment proportions (short coxa stub, long femur, medium tibia, short tarsus) are anatomical inference per protocol #8. Leg pair I (front) and IV (rear) read longest from top-view tip spread (~x2-23, full 20+ unit span), pairs II/III shorter and more laterally directed, matching the top-view silhouette. All y-directions for legs are negative (down) per the mandatory sign flip, since ground (y~15.5 screen) lies below the cephalothorax attachment (y~8 screen). Left/Right leg copies mirror only in the z-component (+z = animal's left), lengths kept identical per pair to encode proportion rather than the current mid-stride pose. Root placed at length 0 with direction [0,0,0] as required.

tree.notes: Crab carapace modeled as two spine nodes (fore/aft) off a central root for structural variety. Rostrum serves as the 'head' leaf (crabs lack a distinct head, it's the front tip of the fused cephalothorax). No external tail leaf included since the crab's abdomen/apron is folded flat underneath and not a protruding terminal appendage. Chelipeds (claws) split into merus/carpus/claw based on side and front view bend points; claws read as raised above the body (screen-y decreasing => positive actual dy after sign flip). The four walking-leg pairs are shown at different stride phases in the render (classic mid-walk pose) but are authored with identical thigh/shank/foot lengths (5/5/4) per the proportion-not-pose rule, attaching at three points along the spine (fore_carapace, root, aft_carapace) to reflect their front-to-rear body position. All leg chains have monotonically negative dy from hip to foot, consistent with the flipped-grid convention (ground = large screen-y = downward in actual frame).

Vertical axis sign was flipped from the on-screen grid (down-screen => negative y) throughout, e.g. all leg 'foot' directions carry negative dy, matching hip-to-foot descending downward.

tree.notes: Raw grid has the head cluster at LOW x (0-8) and gaster at HIGH x (16-24) in the side view, but the top view shows the head-fuzz block at HIGH x (16-24) and gaster block at LOW x (0-8) - i.e. the two views are mirrored in x relative to each other for this render. Since the frame requires +x to point toward the head, all x-readings were mirrored (output_x = 24 - grid_x) before computing direction deltas, using the top-view convention (head = high x) as the reference. The vertical grid axis (y) was flipped per protocol (output_dy = -(grid_dy)) since the grid's y increases downward while the frame's +y is up; every leg segment's dy is negative, correctly sending hip->foot downward. Body spine was split into thorax(root)-neck-head and thorax-petiole-gaster based on the two visible waist constrictions in the side view (x~8-9 and x~15-16). Each of the 6 legs was split into coxa->femur->tibia->foot (anatomical inference of ant leg segmentation, analogous to thigh->knee->shank->hock->foot) since only attachment point and ground-contact tip are directly visible; intermediate joint count is inferred, not directly read. Antennae and mandibles are treated as sub-flap detail of the head leaf, not separate leaves, per protocol.

tree.notes: Side view's wide "batwing" silhouette is the projected shadow of the drooping wing membrane (spans full x-range due to chord length, not true forward/back extent), so forward-axis (x) readings were taken from the top view instead, z (left-right) cross-checked between front/top, y (height) cross-checked between front/side. All grid y-values were flipped (final dy = parent_y_grid - child_y_grid) so descending limbs (legs, tail) have negative dy as required. Tail split into tail_mid/tail_tip and legs split with an inferred knee joint per the joint-chain convention; bat legs are largely hidden in the wing membrane in all views so knee/foot positions are proportionally inferred (shorter than the clearly-visible tail). Wing elbow/wrist joints are inferred by interpolating along the shoulder->wingtip vector read from the top view. Ears/eyes are sub-flap detail folded into the head leaf, not separate leaves.
